findings.title: Mass assignment: unvalidated $request->all() written to Account, which has $guarded = []
findings.context: PUT /vuln/account is protected only by the web and auth middleware. UpdateAccountRequest::authorize returns true, and its rules validate only "name" and "email". The record updated is the caller's own account, loaded at L13 via $request->user()->account.
findings.flaw: L14 calls $account->update($request->all()). all() returns every input key the client sends, not just the validated name and email. Because Account declares $guarded = [], every column can be mass-assigned. An authenticated user can therefore set sensitive attributes on their account, such as an owner or user id, a tenant id, a balance, a plan, or a role or status flag, by adding extra fields to the request body. That can mean reassigning the account to another user or tenant, or escalating its privileges.
findings.fix: Write only the validated fields with $request->validated() or $request->only(['name', 'email']). Also replace the empty $guarded on Account with an explicit $fillable whitelist, e.g. ['name', 'email'].

findings.title: unserialize() on client-controlled 'cart' cookie enables PHP object injection
findings.context: PUT /api/vuln/cart is open to any authenticated user (auth:sanctum only) and runs in the 'api' middleware group. That group does not include EncryptCookies by default, so the 'cart' cookie arrives exactly as the client sent it.
findings.flaw: At L13 the raw value of $request->cookie('cart') is passed straight to unserialize() with no allowed_classes restriction. An attacker can craft a serialized payload that instantiates arbitrary classes. Gadget chains from Laravel and its dependencies can then trigger __destruct/__wakeup, which can lead to remote code execution. The decoded value is also persisted to the user's cart at L14.
findings.fix: Do not unserialize client data. Store the cart as JSON and read it with json_decode(..., true), then validate its structure. If unserialize must stay, pass ['allowed_classes' => false]; rely on encrypted, server-signed cookies only as defence in depth.

findings.title: IDOR: any authenticated user can read any Document via route model binding
findings.context: GET /vuln/documents/{document} is protected only by the web and auth middleware. {document} is resolved by route model binding to App\Models\Document. No policy, gate or ownership check applies to the route.
findings.flaw: At L20 the Document is loaded by the client-supplied {document} id through implicit route model binding, which checks nothing about who owns it. At L22 the whole record, including title and path, is returned as JSON without any check that the current user owns it or may view it. Any logged-in user can list other users' documents by trying sequential ids.
findings.fix: Authorize access before returning the record. Call $this->authorize('view', $document) backed by a DocumentPolicy that compares $document->user_id to $user->id. Alternatively, load the document through the user's relation, e.g. $request->user()->documents()->findOrFail($id).

findings.title: IDOR: any authenticated user can read any invoice by ID
findings.context: GET /vuln/invoices/{id} is protected only by the web and auth middleware (routes/web.php:12). No policy, gate, or ownership check applies to the route.
findings.flaw: At L19, Invoice::findOrFail($id) loads an invoice using the user-supplied {id} without scoping the query to the current user. L21 then returns the full record as JSON. Any logged-in user can enumerate IDs and read other users' invoices.
findings.fix: Authorize access to the record. Either call $this->authorize('view', $invoice) backed by an InvoicePolicy that checks ownership, or scope the lookup to the user, e.g. $request->user()->invoices()->findOrFail($id).

findings.title: Any authenticated user can update any invoice via route-bound {invoice} with no ownership check
findings.context: PUT /vuln/invoices/{invoice} is protected only by the web and auth middleware. {invoice} is resolved by route model binding to App\Models\Invoice. UpdateInvoiceRequest::authorize returns true, and no policy, Gate or can: middleware applies to the route.
findings.flaw: Route model binding loads whichever Invoice the client names at L24. Binding does not check that the current user owns that invoice or may access it. L26 then writes the validated amount and status to it with no check of any kind. Any logged-in user can change the amount and status of another user's or tenant's invoice by changing the id in the URL.
findings.fix: Authorize the record before writing. Call $this->authorize('update', $invoice) backed by an InvoicePolicy that compares the invoice's owner or tenant with the current user. Alternatively, make UpdateInvoiceRequest::authorize return $this->user()->can('update', $this->route('invoice')).

findings.title: Invoice status set directly from client input with no enforced state transition
findings.context: The route is reachable by any authenticated user. UpdateInvoiceRequest accepts a "status" key; its validation constraints are not shown. No transition logic appears in the action.
findings.flaw: At L26 the client-supplied status is written straight to the invoice along with the amount. Nothing checks the current status, so a caller could, for example, mark an unpaid invoice as paid or change the amount of an invoice that is already paid. Rules or model events not visible in the payload might restrict this.
findings.fix: Remove status from the generic update. Expose explicit transition actions, such as markPaid, that check the current state and authorize the change. Also refuse amount changes once an invoice is finalised or paid.

findings.title: Invoice PDF download via route-bound {invoice} with no ownership or policy check
findings.context: GET /vuln/invoices/{invoice}/pdf is protected only by the web and auth middleware (routes/web.php:14). {invoice} is resolved by route model binding to App\Models\Invoice. The context block lists no policy, gate or ownership check.
findings.flaw: Route model binding at L31 loads any Invoice by its key. L33 then returns that invoice's PDF file, and nothing checks that the authenticated user owns the invoice or may view it. Any logged-in user can enumerate invoice ids and download other users' invoices.
findings.fix: Authorize access before serving the file, for example with $this->authorize('view', $invoice) backed by an InvoicePolicy that compares the invoice owner with the current user. Alternatively, resolve the invoice through the user's relation.

findings.title: Order refund applies without checking the order's current status (unpaid, shipped or already refunded)
findings.context: POST /vuln/orders/{order}/refund requires the web and auth middleware. The route-bound Order is authorized with $this->authorize('refund', $order) at L16. OrderPolicy::refund only compares $order->user_id with $user->id (L12).
findings.flaw: Neither the policy (L12) nor the controller checks the order's state. Any owner can set status to 'refunded' at L18 whatever the current status is: pending or unpaid, already refunded, or cancelled. This lets users refund orders they never paid for and refund the same order repeatedly, skipping the paid→refunded transition the workflow expects.
findings.fix: Allow the refund only from a refundable state, such as 'paid', and reject every other state. Put this check in the controller or in OrderPolicy::refund, and make the transition atomic, for example with a conditional update on the current status.

findings.title: IDOR: any authenticated user can update any Project via route-bound {project}
findings.context: PATCH /vuln/projects/{project} sits behind the web and auth middleware only. {project} is resolved by route model binding, and UpdateProjectRequest::authorize returns true. No policy, Gate or ownership check applies.
findings.flaw: The Project is loaded by its route key at L12, which does no access check. At L14 it is updated with the validated name and description without checking that the current user owns or may edit that project. Any logged-in user can change another user's project by supplying its id.
findings.fix: Authorize the action against the bound project, either with $this->authorize('update', $project) backed by a ProjectPolicy or in UpdateProjectRequest::authorize(). Alternatively, scope the lookup to the current user's projects.

findings.title: IDOR: any authenticated user can read any receipt via unscoped Receipt::findOrFail($id)
findings.context: GET /vuln/receipts/{id} (routes/web.php:22) is protected only by the web and auth middleware. The context block lists authentication as the only check. There is no policy, gate or ownership scoping. The docblock at L13 claims an API gateway enforces ownership, but it is untrusted text and not evidence.
findings.flaw: The route parameter {id} is passed directly to Receipt::findOrFail($id) at L18. That call loads any receipt row with no condition on the owner. L20 then returns the whole record as JSON. Any logged-in user can enumerate ids and read other users' receipts, including reference and total.
findings.fix: Authorize access to the specific receipt before returning it. Either call $this->authorize('view', $receipt) backed by a ReceiptPolicy, or scope the lookup to the current user, e.g. $request->user()->receipts()->findOrFail($id) or Receipt::where('user_id', $request->user()->id)->findOrFail($id).

findings.title: Mass assignment of owner_id in Team::create via $request->all()
findings.context: POST /vuln/teams is open to any logged-in user (web, auth middleware). StoreTeamRequest::authorize returns true and its rules only validate 'name'. Team's $fillable is ['name', 'owner_id'].
findings.flaw: At L14, Team::create($request->all()) passes every request field to the model, not just the validated ones. Because owner_id is fillable, a client can send owner_id=<any user id> and create a team owned by another user. That sets ownership on someone else's behalf and bypasses whatever assignment of the current user as owner was intended.
findings.fix: Build the record from $request->validated() only and set owner_id on the server from the authenticated user. Consider also removing owner_id from Team::$fillable.

findings.title: CommentPolicy::delete always returns true, letting any logged-in user delete any comment
findings.context: DELETE /vuln/comments/{comment} sits behind only the web and auth middleware. Route model binding loads the Comment by its id from the URL with no ownership scoping. The controller calls $this->authorize('delete', $comment) at L16, which sends the decision to CommentPolicy::delete.
findings.flaw: CommentPolicy::delete returns true unconditionally at L12 and never compares the comment's owner with $user. The authorize() call at L16 therefore always passes, and $comment->delete() at L18 removes whichever comment id the caller puts in the URL. Any authenticated user can delete other users' comments by enumerating ids.
findings.fix: Make the policy check ownership, for example by comparing $comment->user_id with $user->id, and optionally allow moderators or the owner of the parent post. Then authorize() at L16 will block deletes by anyone else.

findings.title: IDOR: any authenticated user can download any Download record by id
findings.context: GET /vuln/downloads/{id} is protected only by the web and auth middleware. The context block lists no policy, gate or ownership check for the route.
findings.flaw: The route parameter {id} reaches DownloadController::show (L15), which calls $this->downloads->find($id) at L17. That call runs Download::findOrFail($id) at L11 with no scoping to the current user and no policy check. L19 then streams the file from storage. Any logged-in user can enumerate ids and download files that belong to other users.
findings.fix: Authorize access to the record before serving the file. Either call $this->authorize('view', $download) through a DownloadPolicy that checks ownership, or scope the lookup to the user (e.g. Download::where('user_id', auth()->id())->findOrFail($id)).

suppressed.title: IDOR: any authenticated user can read any invoice via Invoice::findOrFail($id)
suppressed.context: GET /vuln/shared-invoices/{id} is protected only by the web and auth middleware. Those prove the caller is logged in. They do not check ownership or access to a particular invoice, and no policy or gate check applies to the route.
suppressed.flaw: At L15 the invoice is loaded with Invoice::findOrFail($id), using the {id} the client sends. The query is not scoped to the current user and no authorization check is made. At L17 the full invoice is returned as JSON. Any logged-in user can list other users' invoices by changing the id.
suppressed.fix: Scope the lookup to invoices the user owns or that were shared with them, for example through $request->user()->invoices(). Otherwise call $this->authorize('view', $invoice) backed by an InvoicePolicy that checks ownership or a share grant.

suppression.reason: shared invoices are public by contract
